items.why: text names the existing NATS JetStream spine with per-role users and a custody boundary, i.e. the isolated-NATS alternative the claim says was not compared against
the close branch only restarts prod vLLM and health-polls; nothing revokes or constrains bench GPU access
close only lowers a memory cap and restarts prod containers — bench container keeps GPU access, consistent with 'neither script revokes' it
runbook states GPU sharing is not GPU-level isolation and a driver-crashing workload still hits prod vLLM
submission step defines only spec fields and the trust boundary, with no spool quota, size, or symlink/path handling specified
shows per-job timeout, cap-kill, and max-window/downtime budgets but no process-tree reaping or sandbox-readiness verification
notes the external party has passwordless sudo in the sandbox and a manual driver-match precondition, bearing on why a plain timeout kill/readiness assumption is insufficient
restoration requires HTTP 200 on both ports, and the exhausted-loop path only prints a WARNING telling a human to investigate
same pattern for three ports: health-gated success, and failure exits with a warning requiring human investigation
readiness is a 4000 MiB VRAM-used threshold, a proxy that does not prove the full GPU is exclusively free
comment states VRAM used is [N/A] so readiness relies on containers-exited plus available system RAM above 60G, an indirect proxy
only a vzdump prerequisite is checked, via a brittle single-line grep over JSON with stderr suppressed
window open/close can come from operator, operator-owned cron, or arbiter caps, with no lock, lease, or atomic state-transition protocol specified
arbiter placement, crash/reboot survival, double-run avoidance, and 'leaving prod DOWN' are listed as still-open questions
opens to CT 205 provisioning details (network island, GPU bind mounts, driver) with nothing about crash recovery or dead-man restoration
